source.title: Tele-FLM Technical Report
source.authors: Xiang Li; Yiqun Yao; Xin Jiang; Xue-Zhi Fang; Chao Wang; Xin-Zhang Liu; Zihan Wang; Yu Zhao; Xin Wang; Yu-Yao Huang; Shuang-Yong Song; Yong-Xiang Li; Zheng Zhang; Bo Zhao; Aixin Sun; Yequan Wang; Zhong-Jiang He; Zhongyuan Wang; Xue-Long Li; Tie-Jun Huang

record.tranche_reason: Reports held-out loss across training tokens for Tele-FLM and downstream benchmark trajectories during pretraining. These measurements bear on token-scaling and downstream trends, but the study does not fit scaling laws or test compute-optimal allocations.
record.gate_note: The study reports one Tele-FLM validation-loss trajectory as training tokens increase, plus downstream benchmark score trajectories. It does not sweep model size or compute, fit power laws, test small-run extrapolation, or compare compute-optimal parameter/token splits. The cited scaling-law papers and endpoint comparisons with other models are not results from this study on those questions. Training-loss and gradient-norm curves are not held-out loss results.
record.test_reason: This is a technical report for one model (Tele-FLM, 52B). It cites scaling laws (Kaplan, Hoffmann) only as background. Its loss curve is a single run under a cosine schedule set for 2.5T tokens, stopped at 2T. There is no sweep over parameters, data or compute, no fitted functional form, no extrapolation test and no allocation analysis. The downstream curves come from the same single run, with no prediction or fitted mapping. The within-run results cannot show whether any version holds, so they are recorded under fits_no_version. Hyperparameters transfer via µP, which is not a use of the scaling-law claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but it misses the main conclusion. The authors' central claim is that Tele-FLM (52B, 2T tokens) matches or approaches larger models trained on more data, on BPB and benchmarks. They add that µP-based search gave a single stable run with minimal trial and error. They observe that benchmark scores improve as loss/BPB falls. They do not fit or test a scaling law.
record.recipe_differences: Reports a single model's training-token trajectory and downstream benchmark progression, rather than controlled scaling-law fits across model sizes, token budgets and compute budgets.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported training-loss slope typically flattens after 500B tokens; knowledge-oriented English task scores are described as rising smoothly, while reasoning tasks and CMMLU rise more sharply.

fits_no_version.finding: Within one 52B pretraining run, all 8 tracked benchmark scores rise as validation loss/BPB falls. Knowledge tasks rise smoothly; GSM8K, BBH and CMMLU rise more sharply (figure only).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within a single training run, downstream scores improve monotonically with tokens and falling loss, with reasoning tasks showing sharper rises.

fits_no_version.finding: The validation loss of a single cosine-schedule run declines without saturation up to 2T tokens; the training-loss slope 'typically flattens after 500B tokens'.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within-run loss curve shape for a 52B model under a cosine schedule.

record.problems: Only one model and one pretraining trajectory are reported for loss dynamics; the curves provide no extracted numerical points or fitted exponents. No parameter-count or compute sweep, extrapolation check, or compute-optimal allocation test is reported. Downstream trajectories are plotted without numerical values or uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant numeric scaling-law results were left out. Endpoint benchmark comparisons in Tables 5–8 do not show performance trajectories or test the scaling-law versions, so they were not recorded as rows.

untested.parts: No sweep or fit over parameters, tokens or compute; only one run's loss curve.
No extrapolation from small runs to large; µP transfer concerns hyperparameters, not a loss prediction.
No comparison of architecture shapes at fixed parameter count.
No other modalities or regimes tested.
No fitted or predicted mapping from scale or loss to downstream scores; only single-run trajectories.
No comparison of fitting choices or exponents.

record.verdict_notes: The record's 'tests/T2' and its V1/V6 labels are not justified. A single model's within-run curves, figure-only and without fits, cannot bear on power-law form or predictability. The authors' aside, based on Llama3-8B trained on 15T tokens, that 'scaling up the model size is still important' is a confounded cross-model endpoint comparison, not a test of V3.

versions.untested_parts: No fitted power-law form or exponents; no parameter-count or compute sweep; only one model and training trajectory.
No fitted mapping from pretraining loss or scale to downstream performance; only one model's training trajectory and selected benchmark evaluations.

rows.subject: Tele-FLM
rows.operation_detail: Measured validation loss over the pretraining-token trajectory.
rows.locator: Figure 2b, Section 4; loss-curve lesson in Section 6
rows.note: The text says the validation curve generalizes without saturation or overfitting; it also says the loss-curve slope typically flattens after 500B tokens. The plotted trajectory shows loss declining, but no power-law fit or numerical points are reported.
rows.check: One validation-loss trajectory within a single cosine-schedule run (Fig. 2b), reported as a figure only with no fit. It cannot show a power law over orders of magnitude in N, D or C. The 'slope flattens after 500B tokens' remark is about training-loss dynamics and the schedule, not evidence against V1.

rows.check: Benchmark score across checkpoints of one run, figure only. No predictive relation to scale or loss is fitted or tested, so V6 'predictability' is not measured.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Tele-FLM validation loss over its reported pretraining trajectory
reader_labels.reason: The plotted held-out loss declines, but the study does not establish a power-law shape; it also reports that the slope typically flattens after 500B tokens (r1).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: The tracked Tele-FLM benchmarks during pretraining
reader_labels.reason: The authors report that scores improve as pretraining and validation loss/BPB decrease across the tracked tasks (r2–r9).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Reasoning benchmarks GSM8K and BBH, and Chinese benchmark CMMLU
reader_labels.reason: The authors describe sharper increases for these trajectories, rather than the smooth improvement noted for knowledge-oriented English tasks; CMMLU is also said to remain far from saturation (r6, r8, r9).
